page: The Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs spanning 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). The instance features 360 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. The processor cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set support includes AVX and AVX-512 foundation flags, AES encryption, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though advanced extensions like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX are not available. This server does not bundle local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark performance reflects a clear division between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core tests show lower relative performance, including weak scores in single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core evaluations, and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput is substantial, with stress-ng multi-core execution reaching strong benchmark tiers at 70,594.44. Memory bandwidth metrics are notably high, achieving 213.36 GB/sec for large block read operations and 92.34 GB/sec for writes. PassMark extended instruction tests and Redis SET operations (62.03 million operations per second) also achieve strong ratings.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the n1-standard-96 delivers high resource density and robust parallel compute throughput, making it effective for workloads that scale across many cores rather than relying on per-core clock performance. The lack of included local disk storage requires reliance on network-attached storage solutions. Given its balanced 3.75 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, large parallel capability, and high memory throughput, this server is suitable for highly parallel web serving, Redis caching clusters, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose batch processing.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 48 Intel Xeon physical cores with hyper-threading. Equipped with 360 GB of system memory (3.75 GB per vCPU), it lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate weaker single-threaded core performance alongside strong multi-core throughput and high memory bandwidth, reaching 213.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 62.03 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded processing and LLM text generation remain limited, its high core count and memory transfer rates deliver efficient scale for concurrent workloads. The n1-standard-96 is well matched for distributed caching, highly parallel web serving, multi-threaded software build pipelines, and concurrent batch analytics.
